currentContext.strengths: Execution agility as a mid-sized player: platform-led approach enables faster delivery cycles and greater repeatability while retaining scale for enterprise engagements|AI-first culture: approximately 99% of the IT workforce trained in AI, with over 600 ready-to-use agents in Agentverse™ deployed across engagements|Deep, multi-year client relationships evidenced by client concentration in strategic accounts and consistent expansion within existing relationships (revenue per client growing faster than account count)|Strategic technology partnerships including AWS Premier Tier Partner status, AWS Data and Analytics Competency, and Guidewire Migration Acceleration Specialization|Ranked number one in service delivery and among the top three providers for the seventh consecutive year in the 2025 Whitelane Research IT Sourcing Study for the UK and Ireland
currentContext.strategies: Embed AI across delivery and operations through a three-pillar approach: Foundational AI (scalable, secure infrastructure), AI for IT (guardrails-first automation progressing toward autonomous operations), and AI for Business (co-developed agentic solutions with human-in-the-loop oversight)|Expand the global delivery network across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and newer locations such as Egypt to improve resilience and access to talent|Continue investing in proprietary platforms and intellectual property (Tensai®, Amaze®, RapidX®, Agentverse™) to modernize faster, reuse proven patterns and reduce reliance on linear (headcount-led) effort|Strengthen position in Global Capability Centers (GCCs) through the SMC Squared acquisition, combining GCC design/build/operate models with AI-enabled delivery and structured governance|Deepen cybersecurity and identity capabilities through the CyberSolve acquisition to act as a full-spectrum cybersecurity partner with particular strength in identity and access management (IAM)|Build delivery capacity where skilled talent already exists rather than purely on cost — expansion of centers in Coimbatore, Dehradun and Hyderabad (India)|Differentiate on a human-centric AI positioning ('AI-led, human intelligence perfected') with governance, training and human-in-the-loop mechanisms built into platforms and delivery models, rather than treating AI as a separate/experimental layer|Invest at scale in talent upskilling/reskilling in AI and next-gen technologies through HexaVarsity (SONIC certification program, Mavericks campus program, role-based AI cohorts Build.ai/Collaborate.ai/Manage.ai) to sustain delivery capability|For CY26: fully integrate and absorb the SMC Squared and CyberSolve acquisitions into delivery, and mature internally-built platforms (First Steps, Talent Quest, demand-supply matching, Operations Command Center) into settled infrastructure|Board comprises 11 directors (10 non-executive, 4 independent) with a structured governance framework of Board, Board Committees, Executive Committees and management processes; an annual Board/Director performance evaluation is conducted via an anonymized questionnaire-based survey with findings routed through the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. On shareholder returns, the Company confirmed payment of an interim dividend of INR 11.50 per equity share of INR 1 each for the year 2025 at its AGM, indicating an active dividend distribution practice alongside its listed-company governance obligations.
currentContext.expansion: CY25 expansion was footprint- and capability-led rather than physical-plant led, consistent with an asset-light IT services model. Global real-estate footprint: inaugurated a new Global Business Headquarters at 185 Hudson Street, Jersey City, NJ (March) as a hub for AI-led automation, cloud transformation and customer-centric digital solutions; opened a new office at 145 S Wells St, Chicago; opened a new UK Headquarters at Level 32, One Canada Square, Canary Wharf, London (May) as a co-innovation center for its second-largest market; opened a new delivery center in Cairo, Egypt; and announced plans for a major new delivery center in Birmingham, UK, to strengthen presence in the Middle East and Europe. In India, delivery capacity was expanded in Coimbatore (approaching 250 employees), Dehradun (close to 200 employees) and a new Hyderabad center that became operational in February 2026 and is expected to grow to more than 500 employees through CY26 -- centers were sited for access to talent rather than primarily for cost. Inorganic capability expansion: acquired SMC Squared (Global Capability Center design/build/operate specialist) to create a 'GCC 2.0' service line combining GCC capabilities with platform-led AI delivery, and acquired CyberSolve (a global identity and access management specialist with 230+ specialists, 20+ IAM technology alliances and 650+ implementations) to deepen cybersecurity/IAM capability. R&D/platform build-out: continued investment in proprietary platforms Amaze, Tensai, RapidX and Agentverse (600+ ready-to-use AI agents); R&D running large-scale AI model fine-tuning on the company's own GPU clusters, and robotics/intelligent-systems experimentation using NVIDIA Isaac Lab training environments.
currentContext.mdna: Growth in CY25 was broad-based rather than concentrated in one vertical or geography, with Financial Services, Travel and Transportation, Banking, and Healthcare and Insurance growing significantly and the Americas growing 9.5%|Revenue growth was driven largely by volume increase rather than pricing|Client relationships are deepening and scaling: two accounts crossed USD 100 Mn in annual revenue (up from one in CY24) and four crossed USD 50 Mn (up from three), reflecting deeper integration into clients' transformation programs and revenue per client growing faster than account count|Structural demand tailwinds cited: worldwide IT spending reaching USD 5.54 trillion in CY25 (strongest growth in ~30 years per Gartner) driven by GenAI/data-center buildout; IT services outsourcing market estimated at USD 662 Bn in CY25 growing to USD 1.35 trillion by CY34; digital transformation spend approaching USD 4 trillion by CY27 (IDC)|Client demand themes: AI-led transformation moving from pilots to production-grade deployment; cloud modernization shifting from 'whether' to 'how to run cloud well'; cybersecurity/identity modernization as a growing anchor spend area; GCCs increasingly used for strategic capabilities (product engineering, data/AI, cybersecurity) rather than just cost arbitrage|Opportunity set: GenAI moving from pilots to scale, hybrid/multi-cloud modernization, cybersecurity/identity/resilience (IAM market projected to reach ~USD 100 Bn by CY33), sustainability-linked technology decisions, GCC build-operate services, and responsible AI governance as a differentiator|Headwinds flagged: macro uncertainty lengthening decision cycles for discretionary projects, pricing pressure and vendor consolidation, insourcing/client-built models (GCCs, internal AI teams) shifting scope away from vendors|Revenue quality improving alongside volume: two client accounts crossed USD 100 Mn in annual revenue (up from one in CY24) and four crossed USD 50 Mn (up from three), indicating growing scale and depth of existing client relationships as a source of forward revenue visibility

risks.risk: Macro uncertainty and longer decision cycles
risks.note: Economic uncertainty can slow client decision-making and push out timelines for discretionary technology projects even when business cases are strong.
Clients seeking more value at lower cost and reducing the number of vendors they work with increases competitive intensity and makes pricing discussions more challenging.

A significant proportion of executives report bringing previously outsourced work back in-house; expanded client GCCs and internal AI/engineering teams can shift scope away from external providers like Hexaware.
As AI becomes embedded in delivery, errors or weak controls in AI systems can create operational, reputational or regulatory issues, requiring ongoing investment in governance and quality.
Data protection and AI-related regulations continue to evolve; combined with rising cyber threats, this raises the bar on security capabilities, compliance monitoring and third-party risk management.
Demand for skills in AI, cloud, security and modern engineering remains high; sustained reskilling, upskilling and retention are required to keep pace with client needs.

risks.risk: Geographic revenue concentration in the Americas
risks.note: The Americas contributed 75.3% of revenue share versus 19% Europe and 5.8% Asia-Pacific, leaving the business heavily exposed to demand and macro conditions in a single region.

Large global IT services firms, specialist boutiques, hyperscalers, platform vendors and clients' own GCCs all compete for similar technology budgets, with clients evaluating not just capability but who takes accountability for outcomes.

one-line thesis: Hexaware reported a sequential revenue decline driven by seasonal furloughs, calendar effects, and a specific GSE budget cut, masking robust underlying deal wins including a major Big Tech consolidation opportunity. While Q1 FY27 faces margin compression from rebadging and utilization ramp-ups, the company guides for full-year growth acceleration above 7.6% as new AI-enabled services and large deal ramp-ups materialize in H2.
financial scorecard: Revenue $389M (-1.5% QoQ, +7.6% YoY); Reported EBITDA margin 17% (Normalized 15.4%, -210bps QoQ due to forex, calendar, utilization, merit hikes); PAT impacted by $25M earnout reversal, $15M impairment, $4M credit loss provision, $12.5M labor code charge; Order book/Pipeline crossed $4B; Net Debt Zero (Cash $235M+). One-offs: $25M Softcrylic earnout reversal, $15M client relationship impairment, $4M generic credit loss provision, $3.5M office lease amortization, $12.5M labor code impact.
guidance: Revenue growth >7.6% (CY26) with acceleration post-Q1; EBIT margin 13-14% for CY26 (H1 depressed by rebadging/ramp-ups, H2 recovery); Order inflow strong with pipeline >$4B; Capex not explicitly quantified but focused on capacity building for deal ramp-ups.
order book & pipeline: Pipeline crossed $4B for first time; Key wins: Large Big Tech consolidation deal (right to hunt/RFPs, no predefined book), Global largest pet insurer (end-to-end tech run), Large insurance Guidewire modernization, Global CRO (agentic AI), World's largest casual dining holding co, Large Asian tech services GCC deal, Large PBM product development.
segment / subsidiary detail: Financial Services strongest vertical (sequential & YoY growth); Banking 3rd straight quarter of strong growth; H&I max new logo traction; M&C bottoming out, back to green YoY; HTPS split into Professional Services (trailing, stabilizing) and new TPP vertical (Tech, Products, Platforms); GTT healthy YoY growth; APAC trailing but expected turnaround in CY26.
growth verticals / optionality: AI-for-Business replacing SaaS licenses (Zero License offering); Legacy modernization at scale (2-3 large completions expected); Private Markets vertical launch (new CPO hired); GCC expansion via SMC acquisition; Agentic AI in clinical research and IT operations.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 Normalized margin 15.4% (-210bps QoQ): Forex -20bps, Calendar -60bps, Utilization -60bps, Merit hikes -90bps. CY26 EBIT margin guide 13-14%: Pressured in H1 by rebadging (3 deals) and ramp-up costs, recovering in H2 to exceed current year levels. Labor code change adds ~20bps annual headwind.
capex / expansion: Headcount added +254 in Q4 (10th straight quarter of adds); IT headcount +585, BPS -331; Building bench for deal ramp-ups caused 100bps utilization dip; Total FY headcount +1,535.
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet with $235M+ cash; Strong cash conversion (OCF/EBITDA 76% LTM); No dividends/buybacks mentioned; Focus on organic growth and selective tuck-in acquisitions (CyberSolve integration ongoing).
risks & watch-items: GSE consolidation deal still WIP (70bps full-year headwind assumed); AI productivity dampener on existing scope (20-40% reduction potential); Q1 seasonality exacerbated by calendar and client budget delays; Execution risk on large rebadging deals impacting H1 margins; Macro spottiness in Consumer & Manufacturing.
management quality / tone: Candid on short-term headwinds (calendar, GSE cuts, AI dampener) but highly confident on long-term AI opportunity and deal pipeline quality; Emphasized 'first-mover' status in AI offerings; Conservative guidance to ensure deliverability.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly baked in a 'downside case' for the pending GSE consolidation deal despite being incumbent; The $25M earnout reversal on Softcrylic indicates aggressive initial targets missed due to macro/bankruptcy of two software clients; New 'Zero License' service aims to actively help clients exit SaaS contracts, creating a counter-intuitive revenue model based on replacement rather than license resale.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
